# Studio skills

<!-- Regenerated by `gamestudio skills index`: do not edit by hand. -->

One procedure per deliverable. A skill does not say what a tool does -- the
MCP tool descriptions do that -- it says **in what order, under what
conditions, and how to tell it is done**. Start with `production-routing`,
the index of the procedures.

Agents launched in the studio read `.claude/skills/`. A symlink mirror
`.agents/skills/` makes them findable at a conventional path for agents that
do not read `.claude/`: `gamestudio skills sync` repairs it, `gamestudio
skills check` verifies it has not drifted.

## Studio procedures

| Skill | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| [`animation`](animation/SKILL.md) | Rig and animate an entity in Blender — a skeleton for a creature, parts for a building or a machine — then hand it back to the studio and prove every animation reads. The procedure for the agent that receives an `anim-<entity>.md` brief. |
| [`art-direction`](art-direction/SKILL.md) | Find an art direction, get it approved image by image, train it as a LoRA and lock it into a project's recipe. |
| [`blender-godot-bridge`](blender-godot-bridge/SKILL.md) | Round-trip a mesh between the studio and the user's Blender (retouch, then re-import), or take a studio export into Godot. Not needed for a single Blender or Godot action — call the tool directly. |
| [`character-sheet`](character-sheet/SKILL.md) | Get a reference the 3D step can use — A-pose, isolated accessories, multiple views — with the studio's workbench prompts, then bring a sheet in by splitting it. |
| [`external-image`](external-image/SKILL.md) | Bring in an image made elsewhere (drawing, scan, an artist's concept) and treat it as a studio concept — matting, pose measurement, chosen concept of a card, move to 3D. |
| [`game-survey`](game-survey/SKILL.md) | Bring a studio section — interface, icons, props, mechanics, art direction, VFX, a world section — up to date with what the game already contains, when the project started before the studio or moved on in its code without it. This is what "update the … section" means. |
| [`library`](library/SKILL.md) | Find the path of a produced asset, or rename it and move it elsewhere — within the protections. Deleting is the user's job. |
| [`local-3d`](local-3d/SKILL.md) | Produce a 3D mesh without paying — build the GLB with img2threejs from a reference image, import it into the studio, then derive 2D sprites or an export from it. |
| [`production-routing`](production-routing/SKILL.md) | Pick the studio procedure that fits the deliverable — art direction, roster, reference and sheets, rig and animations, sheet splitting, sprites from a mesh, external image, survey of a section, effects, visual review, library, validation. |
| [`roster`](roster/SKILL.md) | Write or edit a project's recipe and build a batch of 3D entities — style, pipelines, archetype, face budget, sprite settings. |
| [`sheet-split`](sheet-split/SKILL.md) | Split a multi-element sheet (SVG icon sheet, PNG pack, sprite sheet) into one file per element, with a free preview before import. |
| [`sprites-from-mesh`](sprites-from-mesh/SKILL.md) | Render an animated 3D mesh into 2D sprite sheets — one per animation and direction — choosing the render style, the elevation and the palette. |
| [`validation`](validation/SKILL.md) | Check the studio without spending a cent — lint, tests, and the 3D chain end to end (simulated agent delivery, sprites, headless Godot). |
| [`vfx`](vfx/SKILL.md) | Create a game visual effect — spell, fire, smoke, water, lightning, plasma, magic, impact, explosion — by writing it in the effects language, judging it frame by frame, rendering it to a sheet and delivering it to Godot; then, if needed, hooking it to an entity animation. |
| [`visual-review`](visual-review/SKILL.md) | Check a visual change in Godot — effect, animation, scene — with comparable native captures (before/after, OFF/ON), targeted behaviour checks and a readable record. |

## Vendored third-party material

| Skill | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| [`img2threejs`](img2threejs/SKILL.md) | Turn an object or character reference image into a quality-gated, animation-ready procedural Three.js model built in code. Use for image-to-3D reconstruction, detail-accurate object rebuilds, stylized/likeness-maximized human characters, sculpt specs, and staged code generation. *(third party — see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`)* |
